title: PILAPS: A Bilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Pragmatic Inference across Phenomena and Settings
abstract: arXiv:2611.25459v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent work reports strong pragmatic performance by large language models (LLMs) in English, yet whether this performance generalises across languages and evaluation settings remains unclear. This question is increasingly important as LLMs are deployed across languages, cultures, and conversational contexts. In this paper, we first introduce PILAPS, a bilingual English/Mandarin Chinese benchmark covering eight pragmatic phenomena across purpose-written and dialogue-derived items, with both culturally adapted and independently sourced data. We then evaluate eight LLMs from four families across a range of model sizes and prompting strategies. Our results reveal substantial variation across models and pragmatic phenomena: open-source models continue to struggle particularly with humour, while cross-linguistic performance varies with model origin. translated_title: PILAPS：一个跨语用现象与跨评估场景的双语语用推理评测基准
translated_abstract: 近期研究报道大型语言模型（LLM）在英语语用任务上表现优异，但这种表现能否推广到其他语言和评估设置仍不清楚。随着LLM被部署到不同语言、文化和对话情境中，这一问题日益重要。本文首先提出了PILAPS，一个英语/普通话双语基准，涵盖八种语用现象，包括专门编写的条目和源自真实对话的条目，同时包含文化适配数据和独立来源数据。随后，我们评估了来自四个模型家族的八个LLM，涵盖多种模型规模和提示策略。结果显示，不同模型和不同语用现象之间存在显著差异：开源模型在幽默理解方面尤为困难，而跨语言表现随模型来源不同而变化。错误分析表明，与人类参与者相比，模型更容易做出字面理解。
tldr: 该论文提出了首个英语/普通话双语语用推理评测基准PILAPS，通过评估八个LLM揭示出模型语用能力在模型规模、语用现象和语言间存在显著差异，尤其开源模型在幽默理解上表现薄弱。
